+1 to engaging on this; BrightWave is strategic for our analytics vertical. Recommendation below (keeps runway while protecting revenue):

Proposed structure (sales recommendation):
- Pilot period: 15% credit applied as invoice credit for pilot months (to get them started).
- MAP checkpoint (month 3): if milestones met, release additional 5% credit (total 20% applied retroactively).
- Commit/ramp milestone (within 12 months): if customer hits $200k ARR ramp target, issue a final 10% rebate (bringing effective to 30%), paid as a one-time credit or rebate on invoices.
- Clawback: any failure to meet ramp results in prorated recoupment over 12 months (language to be drafted by Legal).

Approval path: Sales manager sign-off (me) OK for up to 20% total credit; anything >20% needs VP + CFO sign-off; a permanent price change is NOT on the table — must be credits/rebates. If finance is comfortable with credit treatment I say we offer the above and ask for procurement to confirm acceptance of credit-based model.

I will draft a short term sheet (MAP_TermSheet.xlsx) and drop it here for review. Planning to move to VP escalation only if the customer pushes for >20%.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Sales

Subject: Re: BrightWave evaluation plan & conditional rebate request — finance input

Thanks for the context. Finance perspective: we can accept milestone-based credits (bill-back credits) rather than list-price reductions, but we need clear triggers and repayment mechanics. Constraints and decisions:

- Authorization: I will approve up to 20% total as invoice credits for the pilot/early MAP stages. Any commitment that produces >20% effective discount or that impacts ARR recognition beyond credits requires CEO sign-off.
- Risk control: credits must be recorded as contra-revenue and we need an auditable milestone table. Naomi — Legal should include a clawback clause that allows us to recoup credits pro rata if ramp targets are missed and to perform an audit of usage metrics.
- Recommendation: include a capped credit pool and a payment schedule: 15% initially, +5% at checkpoint, +10% final rebate upon validated ramp, but final 10% only released after finance validation of ARR.

I can sign the approval memo for up to 20% today; if Sales wants to push to 30% effective (as Sam requested), we need a short note for CEO review (I'll prepare impact numbers). Provide me the MAP_TermSheet and a short executive summary and I'll route for quick CEO approval if necessary.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

Sam — thanks for the quick reply and for sharing procurement constraints. Per internal review:

- We can offer a milestone-based credit structure rather than a list-price change. The short form proposal:
  * Pilot credit: 15% invoice credit during pilot months.
  * MAP checkpoint (month 3): additional 5% credit retroactively applied if milestones validated (total 20%).
  * Commit/ramp validated (within 12 months, $200k ARR target): one-time 10% rebate (final effective 30%) — final rebate issued after finance validation per agreed audit process.
  * Clawback: prorated recoupment language to be included in SOW if ramp targets are not met.

- Rishi (VP Finance) has approved up to 20% as credits; the final 10% that would bring the effective rebate to 30% will be contingent on validated ARR and requires CEO sign-off for firm commitment beyond finance validation.

Attached: MAP_TermSheet.xlsx (term summary) and internal-approval-note.pdf (approval memo).

Next steps: please confirm procurement is okay with the credit-based structure and the staged release. If yes, we will produce a short SOW addendum with the credit/clawback language and circulate for DocuSign. If BrightWave still needs >20% guaranteed without performance validation, let me know and I will escalate for CEO review (this will add a 48–72 hour turnaround).

Best,
